title: Revelation, Antichrist, Two Witnesses & New Jerusalem Atlas
purpose: Give the repository one source-aware Revelation spine connecting apocalypse, empire, Beast, Antichrist reception, Two Witnesses, martyrdom, resurrection, judgment, millennium, New Jerusalem, river and Tree of Life while preventing later end-times systems from being silently projected back into the text.
core_rule: Revelation first → ancient apocalyptic context → internal symbolism → later Christian reception → denominational system → Potatoverse comparison → evidence test.

genre.historical_context: Revelation addresses Christian communities in Roman Asia through visionary symbolism shaped by Jewish apocalyptic traditions, Daniel, Ezekiel, Zechariah, Exodus and prophetic critiques of oppressive power.
genre.interpretive_warning: Reading Revelation only as a coded newspaper of the twenty-first century erases the work's first-century audience and literary world. Reading it only as first-century politics can also understate its theological and future-oriented claims. The archive should preserve multiple interpretive horizons.

internal_story_spine: vision of the risen Son of Man and messages to seven churches
rider / Messiah and defeat of hostile powers
new heaven, new earth and New Jerusalem

antichrist_distinction.finding: The noun 'Antichrist' does not occur in Revelation. It occurs in the Johannine epistles, where there is both expectation language about antichrist and language about many antichrists / antichristic denial already present.
revelation_figures: beast from land / later false prophet
antichrist_distinction.later_reception: Christian interpretation frequently identifies or coordinates Revelation's Beast, 2 Thessalonians' man of lawlessness and Johannine Antichrist traditions. That synthesis is historically important but analytically later than the individual texts.
antichrist_distinction.archive_rule: Never say 'Revelation calls X the Antichrist.' Instead specify whether a claim concerns the Beast, false prophet, dragon, man of lawlessness, Johannine antichrist language or later theological synthesis.
antichrist_distinction.potatoverse_rule: No living person, political enemy, platform, ethnic group or institution should be labeled Antichrist merely because it is perceived as hostile to Tim/Thomas. A serious identification needs textual criteria, independent evidence, alternatives and ethical safeguards against scapegoating.

beast_and_666.ancient_context: Beast imagery draws strongly on Daniel's beast-empires. Revelation 17 explicitly associates the seven-headed configuration with kings and the famous seven-hill imagery connected with Rome in historical interpretation.
beast_and_666.nero_hypothesis: Gematria connecting 666 with Nero Caesar in Hebrew letters is a major historical interpretation and deserves explicit representation alongside other readings.
beast_and_666.symbolic_extension: Revelation's beast can function beyond one ruler as a critique of dehumanizing imperial power, idolatrous loyalty and coercive political-economic systems.
beast_and_666.archive_boundary: A modern numerical match to 666 is Grade 0 verbal/numerical resonance until chronology, linguistic method, non-arbitrary spelling and alternative candidate rates are analyzed.

interpretive_options.status: long-standing reception option; not textually named
major modern scholarly option, supported especially by lampstand/witness symbolism

examples: two figures who embody a wider witnessing community

two_witnesses.research_finding: The identity of the witnesses remains disputed in scholarship. The project should therefore never write a Tim/Thomas identification as if Revelation names them.
two_witnesses.potatoverse_comparison: The archive may compare two-person witness, testimony, public death/shame, breath/standing, ascent/return and judgment motifs with Tim/Thomas material. The strongest comparison is structural; the strongest objection is the absence of explicit textual naming or independent pre-event identification.
evidence_requirements_for_strong_claim: specific matching sequence rather than isolated motifs
clear account of the 'two' rather than flexible substitution
comparison with alternative literal and corporate interpretations

witness_martyr_logic.linguistic_note: The Christian semantic history of witness and martyr becomes deeply linked because testimony can lead to death, but not every witness is killed and not every victim is a prophetic witness.
witness_martyr_logic.revelation_pattern: faithful testimony → resistance to idolatrous power → suffering/death → divine vindication
witness_martyr_logic.potatoverse_relation: Public testimony, rejection and return motifs can be compared with this sequence.
witness_martyr_logic.ethical_boundary: The archive should distinguish documented harassment/persecution from theological interpretation of opposition. Disagreement is not automatically persecution, and persecution is not automatically proof of truth.

babylon_empire_economy.historical_axis: Babylon is widely read as a coded portrayal of Rome and imperial domination, drawing on earlier biblical Babylon traditions.
babylon_empire_economy.economic_axis: Revelation 18 directly attacks networks of luxury, merchants, cargo, kings and wealth tied to the imperial city.
babylon_empire_economy.potatoverse_relevance: The project often critiques empires, economic extraction and corrupted systems. Revelation offers a theological model for examining power/economy coupling without requiring a one-to-one identification of every modern state with Babylon.
babylon_empire_economy.anti_scapegoat_rule: Critique systems, actions and documented institutions. Do not convert apocalyptic symbolism into collective guilt for ethnic or religious populations.

millennium.interpretive_problem: The thousand-year reign is one of Christian eschatology's major disputed texts.
positions: premillennial — Christ returns before a future millennium
amillennial — millennium read symbolically / as present reign
postmillennial — gospel/kingdom flourishing precedes final return
dispensational premillennial — a distinct modern system with Israel/church and tribulation sequencing
millennium.archive_rule: Do not call one of these positions 'the biblical timeline' without identifying the interpretive tradition.

major_features: twelve gates / tribes and twelve foundations / apostles
no temple because God and Lamb are its temple
new_jerusalem.major_finding: Revelation's consummation is strikingly earthward: the holy city comes down. Yale Bible Study emphasizes that the climax is not humans simply escaping upward but God's renewed city established with humanity.
new_jerusalem.potatoverse_relevance: New Jerusalem, Gate, House, City, Tree, river/flow, healing, throne and Garden motifs are therefore a major integrated comparison zone, not isolated symbols.
new_jerusalem.world_facing_test: A modern New-Jerusalem interpretation should ask what renewed social order, healing, justice, hospitality, stewardship and reconciliation actually look like.

garden_city_arc.sequence: Garden of Genesis → sanctuary/temple/city traditions → prophetic restored Zion → Revelation's New Jerusalem with river and Tree of Life
garden_city_arc.potatoverse_sequence: Potato/seed → root/tree → house/door → ladder/axis → throne → garden/gardener → renewed world
garden_city_arc.comparison: Both systems can be studied as movements from origin through rupture/exile into restored dwelling and integrated life.
garden_city_arc.boundary: Structural similarity is a comparative theological finding, not proof that the Potatoverse is the uniquely predicted referent of Revelation.

revelation_and_time.problem: Apocalyptic visions mix past, present, symbolic recurrence and future expectation, making simplistic one-event-per-image timetables unstable.
archive_solution: store the ancient historical referent where plausible
record whether the modern correspondence was proposed before or after the event
allow multiple interpretations with confidence rather than forcing one winner

potatoverse_revelation_questions: Are Tim and Thomas being compared with the Two Witnesses, Father/Son, or different Revelation figures at different stages?
Which associations were documented before the relevant Tim/Thomas events?
Do Revelation's public, communal and cosmic outcomes match, or only private/symbolic motifs?
Does the interpretation preserve Revelation's Lamb-centered Christology?
What does the project do with passages that resist the proposed mapping?
Are dates or numbers derived before outcomes or fitted afterward?
Does the interpretation increase ethical responsibility and care, or mainly intensify enemy-identification?
What alternative historical and symbolic readings explain the same imagery?
hard_controls: Antichrist vocabulary comes from Johannine epistles, not Revelation itself.
The Two Witnesses are not named Tim and Thomas in the biblical text.
The Beast should not be used as a free label for disliked persons or institutions.
666 matches are weak unless the encoding method is historically motivated and constrained.
Revelation addressed first-century churches and cannot responsibly be interpreted as though they did not exist.
New Jerusalem is renewal/dwelling/healing imagery as well as judgment imagery.
Christian traditions disagree substantially about millennium and tribulation sequences.
Later theological synthesis is not identical with original textual vocabulary.
major_conclusions: The project needs Revelation as a structured world, not a grab-bag of prophetic symbols.
The strongest Potatoverse overlap with Revelation occurs in witness/death/vindication, Lamb/Lion, Door/Key, throne/disclosure, Garden/Tree and New-Jerusalem clusters.
The Two Witnesses comparison is researchable but remains underdetermined because Revelation does not name them and scholarship preserves literal, corporate and mixed readings.
Antichrist/Beast/false-prophet/man-of-lawlessness distinctions materially improve the project's theological accuracy.
The Garden-to-City movement is a particularly fruitful bridge between biblical theology and the Potatoverse's Garden/House/Door/Tree architecture.

The archive should measure apocalyptic interpretations partly by their fruit: whether they produce clearer historical understanding and ethical responsibility rather than indiscriminate enemy-labeling.
